InboxConfig.description: Settings for the inbox, whichever source its issues come from.

custom_fields.description: Extra Jira fields to fetch (custom fields such as Scoring).

enabled.description: Whether the watcher polls the inbox's sources.

notify.description: Whether to show a desktop toast when a new issue appears.

notify_changes.description:
Whether to show a toast when an existing issue changes status or
priority. Score changes and returns only set the badge.

notify_gone.description:
Whether to show a toast when an issue leaves the inbox
(closed or reassigned). Off by default.

presets.description:
Named cuts of the list, by name: `kasl inbox --preset urgent` lists
what `{"priority": "High+", "since": "7d"}` keeps. Flags given beside
the preset win over its fields.

rules.description:
What the inbox does by itself: when an issue matches a rule's `when`,
its `then` pins it, toasts it as urgent, dismisses it, or tags the task
taken from it.

sort_by_field.description: Field id used for ranking (DESC), typically Scoring (`customfield_…`).

start_on_take.description:
Whether taking an issue also starts it in Jira.

Moves the issue into the in-progress category of its workflow on every
take - from the command line, from triage and from a toast button. Off
by default: it writes to a tracker the whole team reads, and in some
teams "In Progress" means more than "on my list".

toast_snooze_for.description:
How long a toast's Snooze button sleeps: 3d, 12h, 2w.

Shares its spelling with `inbox triage --snooze-for`, because a button
and the picker putting an issue to sleep for different lengths would be
two behaviours wearing one word.

InboxPreset.description:
A named cut of the list, as `inbox.presets` writes it: the flags of
`kasl inbox list`, under their own names.

`kasl inbox --preset urgent` is `--priority High+ --since 7d` when the
config says `"urgent": {"priority": "High+", "since": "7d"}`; a flag given
beside the preset wins over the preset's field. Kept in the config as
written and read here when a command names it, so a misspelt preset fails
the command that asks for it rather than the whole file.

changed.description: Only issues that visibly changed within a window: 1d, 7d, 12h, 2w.

min_score.description: Only issues whose ranking field is at least this.

new.description: Only issues discovered in the last day.

priority.description: A priority name, with `+` for that priority and everything more urgent.

since.description: Only issues first seen within a window: 1d, 7d, 12h, 2w.

sort.description: Order of the list; pinned issues lead whatever the order.

name.description:
What the rule is called in messages, toasts and `show --why`; without
one, its conditions in words.

then.description: What it does to a matching issue.

when.description: When the rule applies; every condition given must hold.

InboxSort.description: What the list is ordered by. Pinned issues lead, and gone then dismissed issues trail, whatever the key.
enumDescriptions: Ranking field descending, then priority - the inbox's own order.
Most recently changed first; issues never changed trail.

JiraConfig.description:
Jira connection settings; passwords are never stored here.

A `completed_statuses` list was kept here until 1.21 for compatibility
and read by nothing: discovery filters by the `resolved` date, because a
status name the instance does not have (English "Done" on a Russian Jira)
fails the whole JQL. It is ignored like any unknown key, and the next save
drops it.

api_url.description: Instance root URL, without the `/rest/api/` path.

JiraCustomField.description: A user-configured Jira custom field for inbox sync / display.

KaslServerConfig.description:
Connection to a kasl-server instance: where to reach it, and how to trust
it.

The agent token is deliberately absent - it lives in the OS keyring, like
every other kasl credential, so a readable config file never carries one.

ca_certificate.description:
PEM file holding the certificate authority that signed the server's
certificate.

Self-hosted deployments are routinely behind a company CA or a
self-signed certificate, which the system trust store does not know.
Naming the certificate here keeps verification on: the alternative -
switching it off - would also accept anyone else's certificate.

pulse.description:
Whether the watcher tells this server, once a minute, if you are
working, on a break, or not in a day.

Off until the employee turns it on with `kasl server pulse enable`:
connecting agrees to send finished days, and a live signal of whether
someone is at their keyboard is a different thing to agree to. It
lives here, beside the address, so the consent belongs to this
connection - disconnecting forgets it, and connecting to another
server does not inherit it.

url.description:
Base URL of the server, e.g. `https://kasl.example.com`. Stored
without a trailing slash so endpoint paths can be appended as-is.

activity_threshold.description:
Seconds of sustained activity required to start a workday - keeps
a stray mouse nudge from opening the day.

min_pause_duration.description:
Minimum pause length in minutes to keep as a pause record; shorter
interruptions are noise, not breaks.

min_work_interval.description:
Minimum work interval in minutes; shorter ones are filtered from
report display.

pause_merge_gap.description:
Largest gap in seconds between two pauses that still counts as one
pause.

A stray keypress in the middle of a break splits it into two records;
pauses no further apart than this are treated as one, so the halves
shorter than the threshold are not dropped. Keep it small - a few tens
of seconds - or genuine short work periods between pauses get
swallowed into the break.

pause_threshold.description: Seconds without input before a pause is detected.

OneOrMany.description: One name, or a list of names meaning any of them.

PluginConfig.description:
One plugin's settings, as `kasl plugin setup` wrote them.

Only the ones that are not secret: a setting its manifest marks secret is
kept in the OS keyring, under `plugin.NAME.KEY`, and never in this file.

settings.description:
The plugin's settings that are not secret, by the keys its manifest
declares.

ProductivityConfig.description: Productivity thresholds for warnings and report validation.

min_productivity_threshold.description: Productivity percentage below which reports warn.

min_workday_fraction_before_suggest.description:
Fraction of the workday that must pass before warnings appear -
early-day ratios swing too wildly to act on.

ReportConfig.description: Report export defaults: output directory and file naming.

filename_template.description:
File name template (without extension) for generated reports.

Supported placeholders: `{date}` - the report date as `YYYY-MM-DD`;
`{seq}` - empty for the day's first report, then `_2`, `_3` and so on.
The extension follows the export format.

language.description:
Language of the labels inside hourly Excel reports: `en` or `ru`.

Russian was the default before 1.0, when the product spoke Russian; the
shipped default is English and this opts back in.

output_dir.description:
Default directory for exports without an explicit `--output`
(created if missing); unset = timestamped file in the current dir.

template.description:
Design template name, read from `<data>/report_templates/<name>.json`;
a missing file falls back to the built-in look.

RuleThen.description: What a rule does to a matching issue.

dismiss.description: Hide it from the list, as `kasl inbox dismiss` does.

pin.description: Pin it, so it leads the list.

tag.description: Tags for the task taken from it.

urgent.description: Toast it as urgent: a toast that stays on screen until acted on.

RuleWhen.description: When a rule applies. Every given condition must hold; a list means any of it.

min_score.description: The ranking field (e.g. Scoring) at least this.

priority.description: A priority name, with `+` for that priority and everything more urgent.

project.description: Projects (in Jira, the prefix of the key).

SiConfig.description: SiServer connection settings; auth and API live on separate hosts.

api_url.description: Base URL for reports and calendar data.

TaskDiscoveryConfig.description: Settings for intelligent task discovery (`kasl task find`).

ignore_names.description:
Names/prefixes of tasks and commits to exclude from discovery.

Matching is case-insensitive after normalization; a pattern matches
when the candidate name equals it or starts with it.

description: kasl's settings file: config.json in kasl's data directory.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows. kasl writes it, so an editor checks every key.

inbox.description:
The inbox: how often its sources are polled, what it toasts, its rules.

Written `jira_inbox` before v1.19, when Jira was its only source; a
file with the old key is read as it is and saved under the new one.

kasl_server.description:
kasl-server: the team server this agent reports to. Written by `kasl
server connect`.

plugins.description:
What each plugin has been told, by its name (`gitlab` for
`kasl-plugin-gitlab`). A plugin is used because it is installed, not
because it is listed here; this holds only its settings. Written by
`kasl plugin setup NAME`.

si.description:
SiServer, the corporate reporting API: `report --send` and the
company's rest days.

task_discovery.description: Task discovery ignore list; built-in defaults apply when absent.
